title: MongoDB queries for the app
summary: Find the top scorers with sort and limit, and compute department averages with an aggregation pipeline.

quiz.q: Which sort puts the highest marks first?
quiz.explain: -1 means descending (largest first) and 1 means ascending.

quiz.q: Complete the group stage that averages marks for each department.
quiz.explain: `_id` names what to group by, written as `'$field'`. `$avg` calculates the mean of each group.

quiz.q: Arrange the stages to get only the single best department, with its average.
quiz.explain: Each stage works on the output of the one before it. Sorting by `average` only works after `$group` has created that field, and `$limit` must come after the sort so that it keeps the best bucket.

quiz.q: How many documents does this return when 10 students exist?
quiz.explain: `limit(3)` stops after three documents, whatever the collection size.

exercise.task:
Write two queries in `query.js`. Students have `name`, `department` and `marks`.

- Query 1: `find` students with **75 or more** marks, sorted by marks **highest first**, limited to **3**.
- Query 2 (last statement): an `aggregate` that returns one row per department as `{ department, average }`, with the highest average first. Do not return `_id`.
hints: Chain the cursor methods on find: `.sort(...)` and then `.limit(...)`. For the aggregate, the pipeline is an array of stages in order.
Query 2 needs three stages: `$group` with `$avg`, `$project` to turn `_id` into `department`, and `$sort` on `average`.

db.students.find({ marks: { $gte: 75 } }).sort({ marks: -1 }).limit(3)

db.students.aggregate([
  { $group: { _id: '$department', average: { $avg: '$marks' } } },
  { $project: { _id: 0, department: '$_id', average: 1 } },
  { $sort: { average: -1 } },
])
